item.title: Climate risks far exceed what traditional economic models assume, new report warns, citing extremes and tipping points
item.description: A new report highlights that traditional economic models significantly underestimate climate risks, particularly from extreme weather and tipping points. It urges policymakers to recognize these limitations, as current frameworks fail to capture the cascading impacts and systemic risks.

item.title: As told to Parliament (February 5, 2026): Asiatic Lion population in India grew by over 200 in 5 years
item.description: India's Asiatic lion population surged to 891 in 2025 from 674 in 2020, marking significant conservation success. Fire incidents in Punjab and Haryana dropped by 90% in 2025 compared to 2022. Additionally, 6,188 forest diversion proposals were approved, covering 92,063 hectares from 2020 to 2025.

item.title: As told to Parliament (February 6, 2026): Extreme weather hit over 1.3 million hectares of cropped land in 2024-25
item.description: Parliament was informed extreme weather affected over 1.3 million hectares of crops in 2024-25. The government highlighted efforts in rural development, digital agriculture, and health coverage. Sikkim's organic certification faced suspension, while PMAY-Gramin and DAY-NRLM showed progress.

item.title: Future of Africa’s food security: Need investment in technology, data governance, institutional capacity
item.description: Africa must invest in technology, data governance, and institutional capacity to enhance food security, according to a new report. By leading in AI, geospatial tools, and aquaponics, Africa can address climate change, improve rural livelihoods, and create economic opportunities.

item.title: Drastic seaweed growth threatens marine life and fishing — but also offers opportunities
item.description: Rising seaweed blooms, driven by warming seas and nutrient pollution, are disrupting marine life and coastal economies globally. While they offer potential benefits, such as carbon absorption and resource use, their excessive growth poses significant challenges to fisheries, wildlife, and tourism.

item.title: African climate science-policy has a serious blind spot: Slowing Atlantic circulation
item.description: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation's rapid slowdown poses severe climate risks for Africa, including increased warming and extreme weather. Scientists call for urgent research and policy updates to address this oversight in African climate strategy.
